source_note: Every country cites its European Commission eInvoicing Country Factsheet (2026 edition). Countries whose mandates were provisional additionally cite the national legal source, which takes precedence where the factsheet lags — see notes for Norway, Slovenia and Spain in particular.

countries.name: Austria

phases.applies_to: All suppliers, including foreign ones, invoicing central government
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Central government requires supplier issuance via e-Rechnung.gv.at / USP; sub-central adoption is voluntary. Two national CIUS apply.

countries.name: Belgium

phases.applies_to: Public contracts of EUR 215,000 or more
Public contracts of EUR 30,000 or more
Public contracts below EUR 30,000 (contracts under EUR 3,000 exempt)
All VAT-liable Belgian entities, for domestic transactions

countries.notes: Peppol is the exclusive route; an emailed PDF no longer satisfies the B2B obligation. Exemptions: entities registered for Belgian VAT only, certain VAT-exempt entities, bankrupt entities, and flat-rate scheme taxpayers. B2C is out of scope.

countries.name: Bulgaria

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Article 115a of the Public Procurement Act
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: A public consultation has been opened on adopting a mandatory clearance model along Italian/French lines; nothing adopted.

countries.name: Cyprus

phases.applies_to: Central public sector bodies
Sub-central entities
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Supplier issuance is voluntary. Mandatory B2B/B2C is a stated long-term objective with no timeline.

countries.name: Czechia

phases.applies_to: Public contracting authorities, under Act No. 134/2016 on Public Procurement
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: B2G runs through the NEN platform. ISDOC is the national format alongside EN 16931.

countries.name: Germany

phases.applies_to: All German VAT-registered businesses
Businesses with annual turnover above EUR 800,000
All remaining businesses

countries.notes: Legal basis is the Wachstumschancengesetz amending §14 UStG, with detail in the BMF circular of 15 October 2025. The receive obligation has been universal since 2025 while issuance phases to 2028 — conflating the two is the most common error about the German mandate. Exemptions include businesses under EUR 22,000 turnover and invoices below EUR 250.

countries.name: Denmark

phases.applies_to: All public contracting authorities (Bekendtgørelse nr. 346 af 15/03/2019)
No B2B e-invoicing mandate. The Bookkeeping Act requires the *capability* to send and receive structured invoices, not their use.

countries.notes: Frequently misreported as a B2B mandate. The 2022 Bookkeeping Act (bogføringsloven) mandates certified digital bookkeeping systems — from January 2026 for businesses above DKK 300,000 turnover, July 2026 for in-house systems — but does not require invoices to be exchanged electronically. OIOUBL 3.0 became mandatory 15 November 2025, with OIOUBL 2.1 phased out by 15 May 2026.

countries.name: Estonia

phases.applies_to: Public sector, for procurement above EU thresholds
Suppliers, on request, where the buyer is registered as an e-invoice recipient in the commercial register

countries.notes: Not a blanket mandate. The Accounting Act amendment works on a buyer's-choice principle: registered recipients are entitled to an EN 16931 invoice by default, and parties may still agree another format. Frequently misreported as a universal B2B mandate.

countries.name: Spain

phases.applies_to: Public entities must receive EN 16931 invoices (Law 25/2013), converted to Facturae via FACe
Businesses with turnover above EUR 8 million (art. 121 Law 37/1992): 12 months after the ministerial order developing the public invoicing solution enters into force
All remaining businesses and professionals: 24 months after that same ministerial order enters into force

countries.notes: Widely misreported in both directions. The implementing regulation exists — Real Decreto 238/2026, published in the BOE on 31 March 2026 and in force since 20 April 2026 — so 'awaiting the regulation' is out of date. But it still sets no calendar date: obligations become enforceable 12 months (above EUR 8M turnover) and 24 months (everyone else) after the *ministerial order* governing the AEAT public invoicing solution enters into force, and that order is still pending. The 2025-2027 dates in circulation are wrong; commonly cited estimates now point at late 2027 and late 2028. VERIFACTU and SII are separate regimes.

countries.name: Finland

phases.applies_to: Central government bodies, under the eInvoicing Act 241/2019
No mandate. Under Act 241/2019 businesses above EUR 10,000 turnover hold a right to request an EN 16931 invoice — an entitlement, not an obligation to use e-invoicing.

countries.notes: Finland's B2G scope goes beyond the Directive minimum to national thresholds.

countries.name: France

phases.applies_to: Public authorities must receive and process EN 16931 invoices (Chorus Pro)
All businesses must be able to receive e-invoices
Large enterprises and mid-caps
SMEs and micro-enterprises

countries.notes: Legal basis is Article 26 of the 2022 amending finance law. Since October 2024 the state portal (PPF) no longer handles B2B invoice exchange — invoices route through accredited private platforms (PDP), with Chorus Pro acting as directory and data concentrator. DGFiP became the Peppol authority for France in July 2025.

countries.name: Greece

phases.applies_to: Gradual rollout across general government
General government expenditure above EUR 2,500
No B2B mandate; legislative amendments would be required and no date is set.

countries.notes: myDATA real-time VAT reporting is a separate regime and is not an e-invoicing mandate. KE.D is the central receiving point over Peppol.

countries.name: Croatia

phases.applies_to: All public-sector suppliers (Act on eInvoicing in Public Procurement, OJ 94/2018)
Businesses in the VAT system — issuing and receiving; an eRačun is the only legally valid domestic B2B invoice
Entities outside the VAT system — receiving only
Entities outside the VAT system and the public sector — issuing
Extension to intra-EU transactions

countries.notes: Zakon o fiskalizaciji was published in Narodne novine 89/25, entered into force on 1 September 2025 and applies from 1 January 2026, with system testing available from September 2025. Note the split for entities outside the VAT system: they must receive from 1 January 2026 but only issue from 1 January 2027. eRačun covers domestic B2B only — not B2C, and not invoices to foreign customers. FiskAplikacija is the free tax-administration portal.

countries.name: Hungary

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, for procurement above EU thresholds
Electricity and natural gas suppliers only
No general B2B e-invoicing mandate.

countries.notes: Hungary is routinely miscategorised. RTIR/NAV real-time invoice reporting (universal since 4 January 2021) is a VAT reporting obligation, not an e-invoicing mandate — any format the tax authority accepts may be used. The only sectoral e-invoicing obligation covers energy suppliers.

countries.name: Ireland

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Statutory Instrument 258/2019
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Any future obligation is expected via ViDA rather than domestic law.

countries.name: Italy

phases.applies_to: All suppliers to public administrations, via SdI
All VAT-registered Italian businesses, for domestic transactions

countries.notes: The EU's first universal B2B clearance mandate. The turnover-based exclusion for small businesses was removed in January 2024. Exchange is exclusively via the Sistema di Interscambio, not Peppol; Italy's derogation to keep SdI runs to 31 December 2027 under EU Decision 2024/3150.

countries.name: Lithuania

phases.applies_to: All suppliers in public procurement
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: SABIS replaced eSąskaita in September 2024 and is now the only accepted route, connected to Peppol.

countries.name: Luxembourg

phases.applies_to: Large companies
Medium-sized companies
Small and newly established businesses
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Phased B2G rollout by company size, complete since March 2023. Peppol is the backbone.

countries.name: Latvia

phases.applies_to: Suppliers to budget institutions (contracts concluded before 31 December 2024 may defer to 1 January 2026)
All businesses registered in Latvia

sources.title: Grozījumi Grāmatvedības likumā — obligātie e-rēķini no 2028. gada
Saeima adopts amendments to the Accounting Law (5 June 2025)

countries.notes: The Saeima adopted amendments to the Accounting Law (Grāmatvedības likums) as urgent on 5 June 2025, deferring the B2B obligation from 2026 to 1 January 2028. Many sources still quote 2026. B2G has applied since 1 January 2025; structured e-invoicing is voluntary for non-budget entities in the interim. Exemptions cover businesses using electronic tax registration devices, National Health Service systems, and national security agencies.

countries.name: Malta

phases.applies_to: Central contracting authorities and local councils, under Legal Notices 403/404 of 2018
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: No dedicated national e-invoicing platform. B2B/B2G expansion is under study in line with ViDA.

countries.name: Netherlands

phases.applies_to: Central government entities must receive and process EN 16931 invoices
No mandate; voluntary and requires buyer consent

countries.notes: No B2B or B2C mandate is planned nationally; any future obligation is expected to arrive through ViDA rather than domestic law.

countries.name: Norway

phases.applies_to: Public-sector suppliers, for transactions above NOK 100,000 excluding VAT
Bookkeeping-obliged businesses must send e-invoices to one another
Bookkeeping-obliged businesses must keep digital accounts and receive e-invoices automatically

sources.title: Lov 19. juni 2026 nr. 39 om endringer i bokføringsloven (pliktig digital bokføring og e-fakturering mv.)
Nye lovregler om e-fakturering i næringslivet settes i kraft

countries.notes: EEA, not EU. No longer provisional: Prop. 44 L (2025-2026) was passed by the Storting on 8 June 2026 and promulgated as Lov 2026-06-19-39, in force from 1 July 2026 except the Bookkeeping Act changes, which commence 1 January 2027 (sending) and 1 January 2030 (digital bookkeeping and automatic receipt). The obligation was pulled forward a year from 2028 by a government instruction of 16 March 2026. The Commission factsheet still records Norway as having no B2B mandate and is out of date.

countries.name: Poland

phases.applies_to: Contracting authorities, contracts of EUR 30,000 or more (PEF platform, Peppol)
All contracting authorities
Businesses with annual revenue above PLN 200 million
All remaining B2B transactions

countries.notes: Two distinct regimes: B2G runs on Peppol via the PEF platform, while B2B uses the national KSeF clearance platform. The KSeF rollout was postponed from July 2024. Note the phase split — the widely-quoted 1 February 2026 date applies only to businesses above PLN 200 million revenue; everyone else follows on 1 April 2026.

countries.name: Portugal

phases.applies_to: Large companies (250+ employees, EUR 50M+ revenue or EUR 43M+ assets)
Small and medium-sized enterprises
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Legal basis Lei n.º 111-B/2017 as amended. No B2B mandate: PDF invoices remain valid but from January 2026 require a Qualified Electronic Signature. SAF-T(PT) monthly reporting is a separate, long-standing regime.

countries.name: Romania

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Law 199/2020
Taxable persons established in Romania and non-established entities registered for Romanian VAT
All domestic B2C transactions taxable in Romania

countries.notes: One of the few member states with a B2C mandate as well as B2B. Invoices must reach RO e-Factura within five calendar days of issuance. National specification RO_CIUS under Order 1366/2021.

countries.name: Sweden

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Act 2018:1277
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: No B2B mandate and no VAT real-time reporting. Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is used as the national CIUS without modification; voluntary adoption is high.

countries.name: Slovenia

phases.applies_to: All B2G and G2G transactions via the Public Payments Administration
All entities in the Business Register and natural persons performing an activity

sources.title: Zakon o izmenjavi elektronskih računov in drugih elektronskih dokumentov (ZIERDED), Uradni list RS 85/2025

countries.notes: ZIERDED was adopted by the Državni zbor on 23 October 2025 and published in Uradni list RS 85/2025 on 6 November 2025 — it is law, not a draft, and the date is 1 January 2028 rather than the 2027 often quoted from earlier drafts. B2C and cross-border e-invoicing remain optional. The act transposes Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (ViDA). Accepted formats are e-SLOG 2.0 or another established structured standard.

countries.name: Slovakia

phases.applies_to: Central and sub-central authorities, under Act No. 2015/2019
VAT payers established in Slovakia, for domestic supplies to businesses and legal entities (recipients include non-VAT payers); B2G is covered on the same date
Extension to cross-border intra-EU transactions

sources.title: Zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z., ktorým sa mení a dopĺňa zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z. o DPH
sources.publisher: Slov-Lex (Collection of Laws of the Slovak Republic)

countries.notes: Adopted by the National Council on 9 December 2025 as Act No. 385/2025 Z. z., amending the VAT Act (222/2004). Mandatory from 1 January 2027 for domestic B2B and B2G, with a voluntary phase running since May 2026 and delivery over Peppol. B2C is out of scope. Often still listed as B2G-only.
